sentences.text: Adult Kawanectes measured between 3.8 and 4.2 meters in total body length, making it small for an elasmosaurid, a group of marine reptiles characterized by long necks.

This species belongs to the "non-elongated" group of elasmosaurids, distinguished from all others by a unique combination of anatomical traits, including cervical vertebrae that are not extremely lengthened.

Its skeleton features knob-like parapophyses on the caudal vertebrae, an ischium and pubis forming a bony bar with two diamond-shaped openings, a backward bony projection on the humerus end, and a strongly convex femur capitulum.
Researchers propose that Kawanectes exhibits sexual dimorphism in ilium shape, humerus-to-femur size ratio, and sacral centrum proportions.
Kawanectes and its contemporaries in the Kawas Sea appear to have been generally smaller at adult size than their open-ocean counterparts.
The genus Kawanectes was described in 2016 by José P. O'Gorman based on fossils from the "Bentonitas Patagonicas" quarry in Rio Negro Province, Argentina.
Another specimen was reported in 2020 from the La Colonia Formation, and the name combines "Kawa," referring to the ancient Kawas Sea, with the Greek word "nectes" meaning "swimmer."
There are currently 8 recorded fossil occurrences of Kawanectes in the Paleobiology Database.
Kawanectes is classified in the family Elasmosauridae and belongs to the parent group Weddellonectia.
A 2016 phylogenetic analysis found that Kawanectes is a close relative of, but not a member of, the Aristonectinae.
Kawanectes lived in the marginal marine, likely estuarine, environment of Late Cretaceous Patagonia during the Maastrichtian, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
